export const meta = {
  name: 'confirm-post-verification-fixes',
  description: 'Adversarial confirmation of the changes made after the last verification round: dialog handling in the UI, database open pre-check and dev tooling, and the new README sections',
  phases: [{ title: 'Confirm', detail: 'three independent verifiers on private copies of the frozen snapshot', model: '[REDACTED: model identifier B]' }],
}

const S = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad'
const F = S + '/final3'

const RESULT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string', description: 'Verdict for your area in plain words: what holds, what does not, and anything the integrator must know (left-over processes, things you could not check).' },
    checksPerformed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'What you actually ran, with numbers (one entry per group of checks).' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'major', 'minor', 'nit'] },
          category: { type: 'string', description: 'bug | regression | docs | test-gap | robustness | ux | accessibility | tooling' },
          location: { type: 'string', description: 'file:line or URL/command' },
          description: { type: 'string' },
          reproduction: { type: 'string', description: 'Exact commands or steps you ran and what you observed.' },
          expected: { type: 'string' },
          suggestedFix: { type: 'string' },
          reproduced: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true only if you ran the reproduction yourself and saw the problem' },
        },
        required: ['title', 'severity', 'category', 'description', 'reproduction', 'expected', 'reproduced'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'checksPerformed', 'findings'],
}

const COMMON = `You are one of three independent verifiers of a small software project just before it is handed over. It went through a full verification round; the author then changed code, tests and documentation once more to answer that round's findings. Your job is to check exactly those last changes: prove that one of them is wrong, incomplete or has broken something next to it - or establish, with evidence you produced yourself, that it holds. Be adversarial but honest: report only what you reproduced; do not pad the report with speculation.

THE PROJECT
"Multi-Tenant Certificate Admin Console": an internal admin console where tenant admins review course completions, bulk-issue certificates, revoke them and export them as CSV. Backend: Node.js (ESM), Express 5, SQLite in WAL mode (driver better-sqlite3, automatic fallback to the built-in node:sqlite). Frontend: React 19 + Vite. No login: every API request names its actor in the header X-Actor-Email (alice@east.test -> tenant East; bob@west.test -> tenant West). "npm start" installs, builds the UI, creates the demo database and serves UI + API on one port. "npm test" runs 191 API tests (node:test) and then 253 UI tests (Vitest, simulated DOM).
- The task specification: ${F}/SPEC.md
- The project as it will be handed over (frozen, READ-ONLY, 72 files): ${F}/app   (manifest: ${F}/manifest.sha256). Treat every statement in its README.md as a claim to check.
- The changes to verify, as a diff against the state that was verified before: ${F}/delta.diff  (12 files: README.md, backend/src/db/sqlite.js, backend/src/lib/csv.js, backend/test/*.js, frontend/src/components/ui.jsx, frontend/test/detail-revoke.test.jsx, frontend/test/setup.js, frontend/vite.config.js, package.json, scripts/dev.mjs). Read it first.
- The findings of the previous round that these changes answer (JSON, one file per verifier): ${S}/wfres/r4_frontend-browser.json, r4_backend-adversarial.json, r4_test-quality.json, r4_install-docs.json, r4_completeness.json, r4_spec-acceptance.json.

GROUND RULES
1. Work only inside your own directory ${F}/<your-area>/ (create it). Make your private copy first:  cp -r ${F}/app ${F}/<your-area>/app && chmod -R u+w ${F}/<your-area>/app , then run "npm ci --no-audit --no-fund" in it. Never write to ${F}/app, to /home/user/cert-admin-console, to ${S}/final, ${S}/final2 or to another verifier's directory. Check your current directory before every command that starts a server or a dev server: a command typed in the wrong directory has started servers inside the real project before.
2. Ports: use only the port range given to you below. Start servers with PORT=<port> HOST=127.0.0.1 and with DB_PATH=<a file inside your directory> (or --db for the CLI scripts). Never use the default port 3000 unless your area says so. "npm test" needs no settings.
3. This machine has no "ss" or "netstat": to see what listens, read /proc/net/tcp or use ${S}/listening.sh; find your processes with pgrep and /proc/<pid>/cwd. Record the PID of every long-running process you start and stop each one by PID before you finish; check that your ports no longer answer.
4. Node versions: default "node" is 22.23.5 (npm 10.9.9); Node 20.20.2 is at ${S}/node20/node-v20.20.2-linux-x64/bin; Node 24.22.3 is at /opt/node24/bin - put the directory first in PATH to use one, and use a separate copy (with its own npm ci) per Node version. Chromium and Playwright are pre-installed (require('playwright'), chromium.launch() without options). python3 is available. You run as root; "runuser -u nobody -- <command>" runs something as an unprivileged user and "setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override <command>" runs it as root without the right to ignore file permissions. The path ${S} is only accessible to root (mode 0700 above it): for anything "nobody" must read, make a copy below /tmp/<your-area>-... and remove it afterwards.
5. The machine has 4 cores and other verifiers are active at the same time. Do not report a timing observation you could not repeat.
6. A finding needs a reproduction you ran yourself. Severity: critical = wrong or lost data, or an acceptance criterion violated; major = a spec requirement or documented feature fails in a realistic situation; minor = wrong in an edge case, misleading message or documentation, or an important behaviour without any test; nit = cosmetic or very unlikely. What the README lists under "Known defects", "Not verified" or "Unfinished work" is not a finding - unless the README describes it wrongly.
7. Return your result through the structured output: a summary, what you checked (with numbers), and the findings (an empty list if you found nothing wrong).

`

const AREAS = [
  {
    key: 'frontend-dialog',
    prompt: `YOUR AREA: frontend-dialog   (directory ${F}/frontend-dialog, ports 7300-7349)
The change: frontend/src/components/ui.jsx - the Dialog component now uses TWO effects. A layout effect makes everything outside the dialog inert, moves the focus in, and handles Tab and Escape; its clean-up releases the page in the same step in which the dialog leaves the DOM. A separate ordinary effect returns the focus, after the whole page update, to the element that opened the dialog - or, if that element is gone, to the top-most remaining dialog. Before, one ordinary effect did all of it. Also changed: frontend/test/setup.js (waitFor / findBy limit 5 s) and frontend/vite.config.js (testTimeout / hookTimeout 30 s), and three tests in frontend/test/detail-revoke.test.jsx.
Verify in a real browser (Playwright + Chromium) against the real backend, on the production build ("PORT=73xx HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PATH=... npm start" in your copy) AND on the Vite dev server, which runs React StrictMode (API: "PORT=<api> HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PATH=... node backend/src/server.js"; then in app/frontend "API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<api> npx vite --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port> --strictPort"):
1. Focus on open and close, for the certificate drawer (opened from a serial link, from a row click, from the keyboard, from a deep link) and for the revoke confirmation on top of it: where is the focus right after opening; after closing by Escape, the Close/Cancel button, the backdrop, browser back/forward and a changed hash; after a successful revocation (the Revoke button that opened the confirmation no longer exists then: the focus must land on the drawer, not on <body>); after a failed revocation; after "Try again". Does the focus ever end up on <body> or on something behind an open dialog? Is there a visible flash or a frame in which the page behind is operable while a dialog is open, or inert while none is open (sample with a MutationObserver and requestAnimationFrame)?
2. inert: exactly while a dialog is in the DOM. No "inert" attribute left behind after any way of closing, after a render error caught by the error boundary, after switching tabs with the keyboard while a drawer is open (is that even possible?), after rapid open/close sequences (click a row, Escape, click another row, 30 times quickly), after opening a deep link to a certificate of the other tenant ("Certificate not found" drawer), and on the dev build with StrictMode (effects run twice).
3. Tab / Shift+Tab stay inside the top-most dialog; a confirmation whose request is in flight cannot be closed from the page; Escape closes only the top-most layer.
4. Regression sweep of the four workflows on both builds (list with search / sort / paging, detail, revoke with confirmation, bulk issue with outcomes, CSV export), console free of errors and warnings.
5. The UI suite in your copy: "npm run test --workspace frontend" 10 times in a row, then the tests of the describe blocks "Dialogs are modal" and "Revoke dialog: focus and layout" (file frontend/test/detail-revoke.test.jsx) 100 times each under CPU load (4 busy loops) - any failure is a finding, with its output. Check that the new limits do not hide failures: make one test genuinely fail (e.g. expect a text that never appears) and confirm the run still fails, in reasonable time, with a clear message. Check with small mutations that the changed tests really pin the behaviour: turn the layout effect back into an ordinary effect; move the focus return into the layout effect's clean-up; drop the fallback to the remaining dialog - each must fail a test.
Report anything where the browser behaves differently from what the simulated-DOM tests assert.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'backend-tooling',
    prompt: `YOUR AREA: backend-tooling   (directory ${F}/backend-tooling, ports 7350-7399; additionally Vite's fixed port 5173 for "npm run dev" - check that it is free first and free it right away)
The changes:
(a) backend/src/db/sqlite.js: assertFilesWritable() - before SQLite opens an existing database for writing, the file, an existing -wal / -shm next to it and (if one of those two is missing) the directory are checked with access(W_OK); a database this process may not write is refused with "the database cannot be written to (<what is in the way>)" and nothing is created. Connection.assertWritable() (a write attempt inside a rolled-back transaction) remains as a second check after opening.
(b) package.json: the root scripts start node directly ("node backend/src/server.js", "node backend/scripts/init-db.js --reset", "node backend/scripts/generate-certificates.js ...") instead of a nested "npm run --workspace", so that arguments and relative paths (DB_PATH, STATIC_DIR, --db) are taken from the directory the command is typed in; the scripts "serve" and "build" are gone.
(c) scripts/dev.mjs ("npm run dev"): the API (node --watch) is started first and its output is passed through; Vite starts only once the API is listening; a first start that fails ends the command with the API's one-line message and a non-zero exit code; Vite's proxy target follows HOST.
(d) backend/test/helpers.js + acceptance.test.js: the test "a database file that cannot be written to is refused at start-up, not at the first write" now starts its server through launcherBoundByPermissions(): as root with "setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override", else as user "nobody", else skipped with the reason. New unit tests: 'opening the database for the server ends with that question ...', TAB/CR in 'neutralises spreadsheet formulas', a raced mkdir in 'creates missing directories ...'.
Attack each:
1. The pre-check, as an unprivileged process (runuser nobody and setpriv), with both drivers (SQLITE_DRIVER=node): read-only file; read-only -wal or -shm next to a writable file; missing side files in a read-only directory; side files present in a read-only directory (must start); a database path that is a symbolic link (to a writable file, to a read-only file, dangling); a directory given as the path; a new database in a writable / unwritable / missing directory. In every refused case: one line, exit code 1, quickly, and the directory byte-for-byte as before (file list, sizes, sha256, modes). Most important: does the check ever refuse a database that would have worked (false positive)? Think of: a server already running on the same file (side files exist, owned by another user or with other modes), a second server started at the same moment as the first on a new file, the load-test generator or db:reset running while a server has the file open, group-writable files, a file that becomes writable between two starts, root. Run "npm run generate:east -- --db ...", "npm run db:reset -- --db ..." and a second server against a database that a first server has open, 20 times each: none may be refused.
2. The npm scripts: "npm start", "npm test", "npm run db:reset", "npm run generate:east" (with -- --db, --count, --clear, --tenant, --seed) typed in the project root and in a subdirectory (data/, docs/) with relative and absolute paths: where does the file end up; are arguments handed on unchanged, also ones with spaces; is anything created in the project root or outside data/ that .gitignore does not cover? "npm start" on a fresh copy without node_modules on Node 20, 22 and 24; lockfile byte-identical afterwards.
3. "npm run dev" on Node 20, 22 and 24: normal start (Vite answers on 5173, /api is proxied, with HOST unset, HOST=127.0.0.1 and HOST=<this machine's address from hostname -I>); the API restarts when a backend source file is touched and its output still passes through, and a restart that fails while editing (introduce a syntax error, then fix it) does NOT end the command; first start with PORT=abc, with the API port taken, with DB_PATH pointing to a read-only database, with LOG_REQUESTS=2: one line, non-zero exit, no process left (check for vite and node --watch with pgrep), port 5173 free; Ctrl+C (SIGINT to the process group) and SIGTERM end everything with no process left; without node_modules: one line.
4. The suite: "npm test" in your copy on Node 22, 20 and 24 (counts must be 191 and 253, nothing skipped - your copy lives below a root-only path, which is exactly the situation the new launcher is for); the backend suite as user nobody from a copy below /tmp; with PATH reduced so that setpriv is not found (then the nobody fallback or an honest skip message - which one, and is the message true?). Mutation spot check of the changed code (about 15 edits in assertFilesWritable, dev.mjs is untested by design - say what is and is not covered, launcherBoundByPermissions, csv.js): which survive?
Run the backend suite once per SQLite driver as a baseline. Anything that hangs, leaks a process, refuses a healthy database, leaves files behind or contradicts the README is a finding.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'readme-claims',
    prompt: `YOUR AREA: readme-claims   (directory ${F}/readme-claims, ports 7400-7449 - and, for this area only, the default port 3000 with the default database of YOUR copy, because the README's reproduction steps are written for it; check that 3000 is free first, start "npm start" only inside your own copy, and stop it when you are done)
The README changed a lot in the last step (see delta.diff). Check the new and changed text against the running app, as the stranger who receives this repository together with the checklist "README with one-command startup, actor tokens or headers, A1 to A7 reproduction steps, 100,000-row generation, known defects, and unfinished work".
1. "Reproducing A1-A7 by hand" (section 6): in a fresh copy run "npm start" (default port and database), then execute every code block of that subsection verbatim, in order, in a second shell - extract the blocks from README.md mechanically, do not retype them. Compare every output with the comment next to the command and with the prose. Then judge the steps against SPEC.md: does each block really demonstrate what its acceptance criterion asks (A1 isolation incl. "no certificates or audit events written", A2 sequential and concurrent, A3 conflict without a second operation and with the first result intact, A4 issued / skipped with reason / failed, A5 the two reference times and local-date ordering, A6 two filtered and sorted exports under 60 s each, identical, deterministic order with id as tie-breaker, list requests not blocked, A7 one audit event and idempotent repeats)? Where a block shows less than the criterion says, that is a finding. Repeat the run once on Node 20 and once on Node 24, and once with a bash that has "set -e -u -o pipefail" (do the blocks survive being pasted into a strict shell?). Are /tmp/a2-*.json and /tmp/e*.csv left behind - does the README say so?
2. "10. Known defects and unfinished work": reproduce every listed defect as it is described (the 20,000-learner bulk issue that holds other requests up for about a second - build the data with SQL; the linear list search and deep pages at 100,000 certificates: "tens of milliseconds"; the double click in a list row; browser Back during a revocation in flight; netcat and a half-closing client on an export; idempotency keys never expiring; the hint after a refused db:reset on a read-only database). Is each description accurate - not understated, not overstated? Then look for defects that are NOT listed: go through the four workflows and the API once more with that question, and read ${S}/wfres/r4_*.json for findings of the last round that are neither fixed in this snapshot nor listed here.
3. The rest of what changed: the "Where to find what" table (do the links resolve to headings as GitHub would slug them?), the commands table and the sentence after it, the settings table (STATIC_DIR; try it), "A relative path ... is taken from the directory the command is typed in" (try DB_PATH, STATIC_DIR and --db from a subdirectory), the note on the test that runs with setpriv or as nobody, the sentence about leaving with the browser's Back button, the two paragraphs on downloads that cannot be completed, the troubleshooting entry "the database cannot be written to (...)" (provoke each of the three texts in brackets), the label of the sample bulk-issue response, "otherwise idle" in the typical numbers, the test counts (191 and 253) and the Chinese summary at the end (does it agree with the English text?).
4. Consistency: does anything in the README still describe the previous behaviour (search it for "serve", "nobody", "skipped", "localhost", "190", "252", "three of its five")? Do code comments in the files of delta.diff describe the code next to them?
Report every statement that is false, misleading or missing, every command that fails or leaves something behind, and anything a first-time reader would trip over.`,
  },
]

phase('Confirm')
const results = await parallel(
  AREAS.map((area) => () =>
    agent(COMMON + area.prompt, { label: 'confirm:' + area.key, phase: 'Confirm', schema: RESULT_SCHEMA, model: '[REDACTED: model identifier B]' }).then((result) =>
      result ? { area: area.key, ...result } : null,
    ),
  ),
)
const completed = results.filter(Boolean)
const missing = AREAS.filter((_, index) => !results[index]).map((area) => area.key)
log(completed.length + ' of ' + AREAS.length + ' verifiers returned a result' + (missing.length ? '; missing: ' + missing.join(', ') : ''))
return { completed, missing }

completed.summary:
The new two-effect Dialog does what it claims in real Chromium, on both the production build (port 7300) and the Vite dev server with StrictMode (7311, API on 7310). At no MutationObserver or requestAnimationFrame sample was the page inert with no dialog open, and nothing behind an open dialog was ever operable. No inert attribute was left behind after any way of closing I tried: Escape, Close/Cancel, backdrop, back/forward, hash changes, a render error caught by the error boundary, a hash switch to Bulk issue while the drawer was open, 3x30 rapid open/close sequences, and the "Certificate not found" drawer for a West certificate. Switching tabs with the keyboard while a drawer is open is not possible: the tabs are inert.

The tested focus paths all behave correctly:
- After a successful revocation (mouse and keyboard) and after "Close" on an unknown outcome that turned out revoked, the focus lands on the drawer.
- After a failed revocation (422, 500, connection reset) it lands on "Try again". After Cancel following an unknown outcome it lands on the new Revoke button.
- Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the top-most dialog. Escape closes only the top layer. A confirmation with its request in flight cannot be closed by Escape, backdrop or clicks on the drawer.
- Browser Back while a revocation is in flight closes both dialogs and leaves nothing inert.

The four workflows (search, sort, paging, detail, revoke, bulk issue with outcomes, CSV export of 308 lines) work on both builds, and the console shows no errors or warnings beyond the expected failed-request lines.

Test suite:
- 10 full UI runs in a row: 253/253 each time.
- 100 runs of the "Dialogs are modal" and "Revoke dialog: focus and layout" blocks (15 tests) under 4 busy loops: 0 failures, slowest run 31.6 s.
- The longer limits do not hide failures: a test waiting with findBy or waitFor for something that never appears fails after about 5 s with a clear message, and a test that hangs fails after 30 s.
- All three requested mutations are caught. Layout effect turned back into an ordinary effect: 1 test fails (the new MutationObserver test). Focus return moved into the layout clean-up: 1 test fails. Fallback to the remaining dialog dropped: 4 tests fail.

What I found:
- One small regression caused by the change: when the hash moves straight from one certificate to another while the drawer is open, the focus ends on <body> after closing. The previous version returned it to the list link. No test covers this.
- One older defect the change did not fix: clicking the backdrop of the revoke confirmation leaves the focus on <body> with the drawer still open. The simulated-DOM test cannot see this.
- A nit, on the dev server only: one painted frame with the focus on <body> after a successful revocation.

Also seen, older and not counted as a finding: while a revoke request is in flight its buttons are disabled, so Chromium puts the focus on <body> behind the open confirmation. Tab and Escape still work there through the document listener. The code comments say this and move the focus back once the request ends.

Clean-up: everything I started is stopped (production npm start and server, both API servers, both Vite servers, the 4 busy loops), and ports 7300 and 7310-7313 no longer answer. Extra copies are left in my area: appold (the previous ui.jsx, for comparison) and appmut (mutation copy, still holding my experimental backdrop fix in ui.jsx).
checksPerformed: Browser, focus on open and close (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/frontend-dialog/probe/s1.cjs and s2.cjs). The drawer was opened from a serial link, a row click, the keyboard, a deep link and a West deep link, and closed by Escape, the Close button, the backdrop, back/forward, a hash change to the list and a hash change to another certificate: 18 checkpoints per build, on prod (7300) and dev with StrictMode (7311). For the revoke confirmation: Escape, Cancel, backdrop, a Tab/Shift+Tab cycle of 16 presses, failures (422 and 500), in flight (Escape, backdrop, drawer click and Tab all ignored), success via Try again, direct success, keyboard success, and Back while in flight: 19 checkpoints per build.

Continuous check in every run: a MutationObserver plus a requestAnimationFrame loop testing that something is inert only while a dialog is open, that nothing behind the top dialog is operable, and where the focus is. Across all runs: 0 cases of inert with no dialog and 0 of an operable page behind a dialog. Body focus was recorded separately.

Comparison with the previous ui.jsx (from final2) on a separate Vite server (7312). The successful revocation now releases the drawer in the same commit; before, one painted frame showed the drawer still inert. The cert-to-cert hash change returned the focus to the link before; now it ends on <body>.

Rapid sequences (s4.cjs): 30x row click then Escape, 30x link click then Escape, 30x synthetic click/Escape with setTimeout 0, 30x synchronous hash flips, 30x cert-to-cert hash change per frame. Also a hash switch to Bulk issue while the drawer was open, Back to reopen it, and a render error injected after a revocation that reached the error boundary. Every one ended with 0 inert attributes, on both builds.

Unknown outcome (s8.cjs): connection reset without the revocation leads to Try again, then Escape to the new Revoke button; revocation carried out and then the connection reset leads to Close, then to the drawer. Checked on both builds.

Workflow sweep (s7.cjs) on both builds: search (1 row), all 10 sort options, page size and page 2, detail with audit trail, CSV export (308 lines with a header), bulk issue (1 issued, 4 skipped, 0 failed). Console: no errors or warnings except those for the requests I made fail on purpose.
npm run test --workspace frontend 10 times in a row: 10/10 passed, 253/253 each time.
The two describe blocks (15 tests) 100 times under 4 busy loops (load average about 12): 0 failures, slowest run 31.6 s.

The new limits do not hide failures. A findBy that never matches fails after 5017 ms with TestingLibraryElementError 'Unable to find an element with the text: never shown'. A waitFor that never holds fails after 5012 ms with 'expected null not to be null'. A test that hangs fails after 30002 ms with 'Test timed out in 30000ms'.

Mutations, each with the whole UI suite. M1 (layout effect turned into useEffect): 1 failing test ('gives the page back ... in the same step'). M2 (focus return moved into the layout clean-up, second effect removed): 1 failing test ('hands the focus to the drawer when ... the button that opened it is gone'). M3 (fallback to the remaining dialog dropped): 4 failing tests, including one under StrictMode.

Fix check for the backdrop defect: with event.preventDefault() on the backdrop's mousedown, the focus returned to the Revoke button (s3.cjs on a dev server, port 7313). Note the load: the 4 busy loops from the 100-run check were still running.
Clean-up: all PIDs I started were stopped; nothing has its current directory in my area any more; ports 7300 and 7310-7313 return no answer to curl (000).

findings.title: Focus lands on <body> after closing a drawer that was replaced by a hash change to another certificate (regression from the opener being read in the layout effect)
findings.location: frontend/src/components/ui.jsx:179-219 (Dialog: openerRef read in useLayoutEffect, focus returned in a useEffect clean-up); frontend/src/components/CertificatesPage.jsx:333 (drawer keyed by selectedCertificateId)
findings.description: The drawer is keyed by certificate id, so a hash change from one certificate to another removes one drawer and mounts a new one in the same commit. The new drawer's layout effect reads document.activeElement as its opener. At that moment the old drawer's panel has just been removed, so the opener is <body>. The old drawer's ordinary-effect clean-up, which would put the focus back on the list link, only runs afterwards; by then the link is inert and focus() does nothing. When the new drawer closes, it 'returns' the focus to <body>. The fallback is never reached, because body is always in the document. The previous one-effect version returned the focus to the list link in the same steps. This happens when the user edits the URL, follows a pasted link, or uses back/forward across two certificate entries while a drawer is open. The task listed 'a changed hash' as a closing path; no test covers this one.
findings.reproduction: I ran node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/frontend-dialog/probe/s1.cjs against http://127.0.0.1:7300 (prod), :7311 (dev) and :7312 (the previous ui.jsx). Steps: click the serial link EAST-0000006, then location.hash = '#/certificates/<another id>' while the drawer is open, then press Escape. New prod and dev: 'Escape after cert->cert {"focus":"BODY","dialogs":0,"inert":0}'. Previous version: 'Escape after cert->cert {"focus":"A:EAST-LT-0000299",...}', i.e. the focus went back to the link.
findings.expected: After the replacement drawer closes, the focus goes back to the element that had it before the first drawer opened (the list link), as the previous version did.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not capture <body> as the opener. If document.activeElement is body when the layout effect runs, keep the opener of the dialog being replaced, for example in a module-level 'last opener' the passive clean-up hands over. Or treat an opener equal to document.body as missing and fall back to a sensible target. Add a test that changes the hash from one certificate to another while the drawer is open.

findings.title: Clicking the backdrop of the revoke confirmation leaves the focus on <body> while the drawer stays open; the simulated-DOM test cannot see this
findings.description: The confirmation closes synchronously inside the mousedown handler (setConfirming(null) in a discrete event). Its clean-up correctly puts the focus on the Revoke button. Then the browser's default mousedown action runs: the user pressed on a non-focusable element, so the focus is cleared to <body>. The drawer is still open and modal, so the focus now sits behind it, which is exactly what the Dialog docstring and the new fallback code are meant to prevent. Tab and Escape still work through the document keydown listener, but a screen reader loses its place. The drawer's own backdrop does not show this, because its close goes through the asynchronous hashchange event. The previous version behaves the same, so the change did not cause this, but the task asks about backdrop closing explicitly. jsdom's fireEvent.mouseDown has no default action, and the test does not check the focus after the backdrop click, so the suite cannot detect it.
findings.reproduction: I ran node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/frontend-dialog/probe/s3.cjs http://127.0.0.1:7300. Steps: open an active certificate, click 'Revoke certificate…', then mouse.down at (10,10) on the backdrop. Focus trace: [out:dialog, in:revoke-button, out:revoke-button]. After mouse.up: {"focus":"BODY","dialogs":1,"inert":2}, and every animation frame flagged 'BODY focus while dialog open'. s2.cjs on 7300, 7311 and 7312 gives the same result: 'backdrop of confirm {"focus":"BODY","dialogs":1}'. With event.preventDefault() added to the backdrop's mousedown in my mutation copy (dev server 7313), the focus stays on the Revoke button: [out:dialog, in:revoke-button], then 'BUTTON:Revoke certificate…'.
findings.expected: After the confirmation is closed through its backdrop, the focus is on the Revoke button, as it is after Escape or Cancel.
findings.suggestedFix: In the overlay's onMouseDown, call event.preventDefault() when event.target === event.currentTarget. This also keeps the focus inside a locked dialog. Then add an assertion on document.activeElement after the backdrop click in detail-revoke.test.jsx. It will not catch the browser default in jsdom, but it pins the intent.

findings.title: Dev build: one painted frame with the focus on <body> behind the open drawer after a successful revocation
findings.location: frontend/src/components/ui.jsx:206-219 (focus return in an ordinary effect)
findings.description: The focus is returned in an ordinary (passive) effect, on purpose. After a revocation the update comes from a fetch, not a discrete event, so React may paint before that effect runs. For that frame the confirmation is gone, the drawer is operable and the focus is on <body>. On the dev server one such frame was rendered in 3 of 3 runs; on the production build none in 3 of 3. A key press in that frame still reaches the document listener, so nothing can be operated behind the dialog. This is only a single frame of the focus outside the dialog, which is one of the things the task asked to look for.
findings.reproduction: I ran node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/frontend-dialog/probe/s6.cjs http://127.0.0.1:7300 http://127.0.0.1:7311 three times. Dev sequence: '... | mo d=1 i=3 f=BODY | raf d=1 i=3 f=BODY | mo d=1 i=3 f=dialog | ...' (1 such raf in each of 3 runs). Prod: 'mo d=1 i=2 f=BODY | mo d=1 i=2 f=dialog', with no frame painted in between.
findings.expected: No painted frame with the focus outside the top-most open dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Optional. In the layout clean-up, when the focus is inside the panel being removed, move it at once to the top-most remaining dialog. The passive clean-up then refines it to the opener once the commit is final.

completed.summary:
Most of the last changes hold up. I reproduced two problems the changes introduced and two pre-existing ones next to them.

What holds:
(a) assertFilesWritable: every case I tried as user nobody and as root under setpriv, with both drivers, behaves as described. The refused cases are a read-only file, a read-only -wal, a read-only -shm, a read-only directory with no side files, a read-only directory with only a -wal, and a symlink to a read-only file. Each one prints one line, exits with code 1 within 0.1-0.9 s, and leaves the directory unchanged (file list, sizes, sha256 and modes). Healthy cases start: side files present in a read-only directory, a group-writable database with side files from a root server already running, symlinks (including link and target in different directories), and new databases. 20x each of generate:east, db:reset and a second server against a database a server holds open, plus 20 pairs of servers started together on a new file, were never refused.
(b) npm scripts: arguments, including ones with spaces, arrive unchanged; relative and absolute paths resolve from the directory the command is typed in; nothing lands outside .gitignore. "npm start" on a fresh copy works on Node 20, 22 and 24, and the lockfile is byte-identical afterwards.
(c) dev.mjs: normal start works with HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 and 192.0.2.2, and /api is proxied. A first start with PORT=abc, a taken port, a read-only DB or LOG_REQUESTS=2 gives one line, exit 1, no process left and 5173 free. Without node_modules it gives one line. Ctrl+C on a running dev server leaves nothing. A syntax error while editing does not end the command.
(d) The suite gives 191/253 with 0 skipped on Node 22, 20 and 24 from a root-only path (setpriv is used). It gives 191 on SQLITE_DRIVER=node and better-sqlite3, and 191 as user nobody from a copy below /tmp. With setpriv off PATH it gives an honest but vague skip from the root-only path and the nobody fallback from /tmp.

What does not hold:
1. Introduced by the change: the pre-check has a race. When another process closes the database as the last connection while this one starts, assertFilesWritable refuses a healthy, writable database and says a side file is "read-only for this user". It happened 7 times in 40,000 opens, even as root.
2. Introduced by the change: a Ctrl+C at the moment the API comes up leaves an orphaned Vite (parent PID 1) holding port 5173. It happened 2 times in 62 timed tries. The cause is that Vite is now started lazily and passOn() never checks `stopping`.
3. Pre-existing: SIGTERM sent to the `npm run dev` (or `npm start`) process itself leaves dev.mjs, node --watch, the server and Vite running. npm's `sh -c` does not pass the signal on.
4. Pre-existing Node behaviour: after a syntax error in a module, fixing that file does not restart the API; another file has to be touched.

Mutation spot check (26 mutants): 18 killed, 2 of those only by turning the test into a skip. 8 survived. 1 of the survivors (calling the check before mkdir) is an equivalent mutant. The other 7 show missing tests: realpath, the -wal half of the check, dirname(real), every->some, and refusing a read-only directory even when its side files are present. In the helpers, the launcher order, the write probe and startServer's use of the launcher prefix are also unchecked. dev.mjs has no test, by design.

Clean-up: one better-sqlite3 run failed a timing assertion while my mutation runs loaded the machine; it passed 191/191 when rerun alone, so I do not report it. Every process I started was stopped by PID, ports 7350-7399 and 5173 are free, and /tmp/backend-tooling-nb is removed.
checksPerformed: Pre-check matrix: 15 scenarios x 2 users (nobody via runuser, root via setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override) x 2 drivers = 60 server starts. Each run snapshots the directory before and after (names, sizes, modes, owners, sha256); all refusals were 1 line, exit 1, 116-853 ms, directory SAME

Extra pre-check cases: side files present in a read-only directory (another nobody server running): starts with both drivers. Group-writable DB (root:nogroup 0664) with a root server running, second server as nobody: starts with both drivers. Cross-directory symlinks (link in an unwritable directory -> writable target: starts; link -> target in a read-only directory: refused naming the target's directory), both drivers

False-positive loops, a server holding the DB open (root): 20x npm run generate:east -- --db, 20x npm run db:reset -- --db, 20x a second server: 60/60 not refused. 20 pairs of servers started at once on a new file in a missing directory: 40/40 came up
Race harness: 4 processes x 1500 and 4 x 5000 open/close cycles per driver through the real openDatabase(): 7 refusals of a writable database ('-shm ... is read-only for this user')

npm scripts typed in the root, data/ and docs/: --db with spaces, relative, ../ and absolute paths, DB_PATH relative, default path, generate:east with --count/--seed/--tenant West/--clear. File list diffed before and after: only the typed paths plus data/ and node_modules caches are new, all covered by .gitignore

npm start on fresh copies without node_modules on Node 20.20.2, 22.23.5 and 24.22.3: UI 200, API answers, package-lock.json sha256 identical (0292953...); SIGINT to the process group stopped everything

npm run dev on Node 22 with HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 and 192.0.2.2, and on Node 20 and 24 with HOST unset and 192.0.2.2: Vite 200 on 5173, /api proxied, Ctrl+C leaves no process and 5173 free. Restart on touch; syntax error then fix (does not end the command, API stays 502 until another file is touched; same with plain node --watch). First start with PORT=abc (Node 20, 22 and 24), a taken port, a read-only DB under setpriv, LOG_REQUESTS=2: 1 line, exit 1, no leftovers. Without node_modules: 1 line

Signal races on dev.mjs: 23 timed SIGTERMs (0.20-1.30 s) plus 3x31 SIGTERMs (0.30-0.60 s) sent to dev.mjs directly, and 2x31 SIGINTs to its process group: 2 orphaned Vite processes (ppid 1, 5173 taken) after SIGINT, 1 after SIGTERM, plus 2 orphaned node --watch (dev.mjs killed by SIGTERM before its handler was installed)

Suites: npm test on Node 22, 20 and 24 from a root-only path: 191/191 + 253/253, 0 skipped (setpriv launcher used). Backend suite with SQLITE_DRIVER=node: 191/191; with better-sqlite3: 191/191 when run alone (1 timing failure in scale.test.js while my mutation runs loaded the machine, not repeated). Backend suite as user nobody from a /tmp copy: 191/191, 0 skipped

Reduced PATH (/opt/node22/bin only, no setpriv): from the root-only path the test is skipped, with the message 'root without CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE (setpriv) cannot be used or cannot read ...; the user "nobody" cannot be used or cannot read ...'. True but does not say setpriv was not found. From a /tmp copy the nobody fallback is used and the test passes

Mutation spot check: 26 mutants (17 in sqlite.js/bootstrap.js, 4 in csv.js, 5 in the test helpers). Each ran against unit.test.js (82 tests) plus the 13 start-up and maintenance acceptance tests. 18 killed (2 only by turning the test into a skip). 8 survived: M2 no realpath, M3 no -wal check, M7 every->some, M9 refuse a read-only directory even with side files present, M10 dirname(file) instead of dirname(real), M14 check before mkdir (equivalent), H1 nobody tried before setpriv, H2 no write probe, H5 startServer ignores launcher.prefix. dev.mjs has no tests

findings.title: Pre-check refuses a healthy, writable database as 'read-only' when another process closes it at the same moment (time-of-check race)
findings.description: assertFilesWritable first calls fs.existsSync on <db>-wal and <db>-shm and then fs.accessSync(W_OK) on them. mayWrite() treats every error as 'not writable'. When the last other connection closes in between, SQLite deletes the side files and accessSync throws ENOENT. The start is then refused with 'the database cannot be written to (the file X-shm next to it is read-only for this user)'. That refuses a database that would have worked and gives a false reason; it happens even as root. Realistic triggers: a server starting while a db:reset or the generator that had the file to itself finishes, or one server stopping while another starts. This race did not exist before the pre-check was added.
findings.reproduction: Ran as root, no permissions involved. A script that loops `openDatabase(file).close()` using the app's own backend/src/db/sqlite.js (race.mjs, kept as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/backend-tooling/race.mjs). Ran it in 4 processes at once on one database created by init-db.js. Run 1: 4x1500 opens with better-sqlite3, 0 errors. Run 2: 4x5000 with better-sqlite3 gave {"the database cannot be written to (the file race.sqlite-shm next to it is read-only for this user)":1} in two of the processes. Run 3: 4x5000 with SQLITE_DRIVER=node gave 1, 2 and 2 of the same error. 7 false refusals in 40,000 opens; the file was writable throughout.
findings.expected: A side file that disappears between the two checks is not 'in the way': only EACCES/EPERM/EROFS should count as 'cannot write'; a healthy database must never be refused.
findings.suggestedFix: In mayWrite, return true (or re-check existence) when accessSync fails with ENOENT. Only EACCES, EPERM and EROFS should mean 'cannot be written to'. Optionally retry the whole check once.

findings.title: npm run dev: Ctrl+C during start-up can leave an orphaned Vite holding port 5173
findings.description: Vite is now started from passOn() as soon as the API's output contains ' listening on '. passOn() never checks `stopping`. If SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives just before the API's 'listening' line is read, stop() has already killed the known children and set a 500 ms exit timer. Then the line arrives and a new Vite is spawned that nobody stops. dev.mjs exits and Vite keeps running with parent PID 1, holding port 5173. The next `npm run dev` then gets a different Vite port or a confusing failure. This is new with the lazy Vite start.
findings.reproduction: Ran in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/backend-tooling/app (script sweep2.sh). For d in 0.30..0.60 s in 0.01 s steps: `PORT=7375 HOST=127.0.0.1 LOG_REQUESTS=0 DB_PATH=<existing db> setsid node scripts/dev.mjs &`, then sleep d, then `kill -INT -- -<pgid>` (Ctrl+C to the group), then wait 1.5 s and list processes whose cwd is the copy. Run 2 of the sweep showed `0.35 code=0 listening=1 left=[18156:ppid=1:node .../node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js:5173=TAKEN]` and `0.45 code=0 listening=1 left=[22633:ppid=1:... vite ...:5173=TAKEN]`. With SIGTERM to dev.mjs directly (sweep.sh) the same happened at 0.48 s: an orphaned vite.js. 3 orphans in about 155 timed signals in all.
findings.expected: Once stopping has begun no new child is started; Ctrl+C/SIGTERM at any moment leaves no process and frees 5173.
findings.suggestedFix: In passOn, `if (stopping) return;` before spawning Vite (or check `stopping` in run() and refuse to spawn). Also register the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers before the first spawn.

findings.title: dev.mjs installs its signal handlers after spawning the API: an early SIGTERM leaves node --watch orphaned
findings.location: scripts/dev.mjs:41 (run(...) before process.on('SIGINT'/'SIGTERM') at the end of the file)
findings.description: The API (node --watch) is spawned before process.on('SIGTERM') is registered. A SIGTERM that arrives in that window kills dev.mjs with the default action, exit code 143. Nothing then kills node --watch, which keeps running as an orphan. The old dev.mjs had the same order, but the change rewrote this section without fixing it.
findings.reproduction: Ran sweep.sh in the scratchpad app copy: `node scripts/dev.mjs` started directly, SIGTERM sent after 0.30-0.60 s. Leftovers were listed by cwd and printed with their command line. Results: `0.34 code=143 listening=0 vite=0 left=[ 1861:/opt/node22/bin/node --watch src/server.js ]` and `0.36 code=143 ... left=[ 17720:/opt/node22/bin/node --watch src/server.js ]`, plus 1 more in an earlier sweep (0.42 s). 3 of about 93 SIGTERM tries.
findings.expected: No process left after SIGTERM at any time.
findings.suggestedFix: Register process.on('SIGINT'/'SIGTERM') (and the stop function) before the first spawn.

findings.title: SIGTERM to the `npm run dev` / `npm start` process leaves the whole tree running (dev.mjs, node --watch, server, Vite on 5173)
findings.description: npm forwards SIGTERM to its `sh -c` child. That sh exits without passing the signal on, so dev.mjs (or for npm start the server) is orphaned to PID 1 and keeps running. This hits process managers, `timeout npm run dev` and `kill <npm pid>`. Ctrl+C, which reaches the whole process group, works. This is pre-existing npm/sh behaviour and was not introduced by the delta. The README does not mention it.
findings.reproduction: `PORT=7370 HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PATH=... setsid npm run dev`; the process tree showed npm -> sh -c node scripts/dev.mjs -> dev.mjs -> {node --watch -> server, vite}. `kill -TERM <npm pid>`: npm exited with 143, and dev.mjs, node --watch, the server and vite.js were all still alive with port 5173 TAKEN. A SIGTERM to dev.mjs itself then stopped everything. The same with `npm start` on Node 22: after `kill -TERM <npm pid>` the server kept answering 200 on its port.
findings.expected: Either the whole tree ends on SIGTERM to the command, or the README says to stop it with Ctrl+C or a signal to the process group.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `exec node scripts/dev.mjs` / `... && exec node backend/src/server.js` in the scripts so the signal reaches node, or document Ctrl+C / process-group signals.

findings.title: Tests do not cover several branches of the new pre-check and launcher (surviving mutants)
findings.description:
Mutants that survive unit.test.js plus the 13 start-up and maintenance acceptance tests:
- Removing realpath (symlinks).
- Dropping the -wal side-file check.
- dirname(file) instead of dirname(real).
- every->some in the directory check.
- Refusing any read-only directory even when its -wal and -shm exist. This turns the documented 'must start' case into a false refusal and no test notices.
- In the helpers: trying nobody before setpriv, dropping the write probe, and startServer ignoring launcher.prefix. With the last one, the 'with the permissions put right the same file starts' step runs as full root and proves nothing about the restricted user.
Two mutants (probe negated, setpriv without the bounding-set drop) are 'killed' only because the test silently becomes a skip.
findings.reproduction: Ran the mutation runner mut.py (kept as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final3/backend-tooling/mut.py) against a separate copy (.../backend-tooling/mut). For each mutant it ran `node --test test/unit.test.js` and `node --test --test-name-pattern='cannot be written to is refused|root npm scripts|start-up|setting' test/acceptance.test.js`. Survivors with pass=82/13, fail=0, skip=0: M2, M3, M7, M9, M10, H1, H2, H5. M14 (call before mkdir) is equivalent. H3 and H4 gave acc[pass=12 fail=0 skip=1].
findings.expected: At least the 'side files present in a read-only directory starts' case, a symlinked database and a read-only -wal are covered; the final start in the refusal test runs through the launcher.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend the refusal test: a read-only -wal, a symlink to the database in another directory, and a read-only directory where a running server already holds -wal/-shm (it must start). Assert that the final startServer really runs restricted, e.g. that it cannot write a 0444 file.

findings.title: npm run dev: fixing a file that had a syntax error does not bring the API back
findings.description: After a syntax error in a module, node --watch drops that module from its watch list. Fixing the file therefore does not restart the API: /api keeps answering 502 until some other loaded file, such as src/server.js, is touched. dev.mjs correctly does not end the command, but 'API with auto-restart' does not recover by itself after the typical typo-then-fix. This is Node's own behaviour and also occurs with plain `node --watch`, so it is not caused by the delta.
findings.reproduction: Ran npm run dev (PORT=7370) in the scratchpad app copy. Appended `export const x = ;` to backend/src/lib/csv.js: /api via 5173 gave 502 and the SyntaxError passed through. Restored the file: 502 every second for 10 s, and still 502 after touching csv.js again. Plain `node --watch src/server.js` behaved the same: 000 after the fix, 200 only after `touch src/server.js`.
findings.expected: The API restarts once the broken file is fixed.
findings.suggestedFix: Start the API with `node --watch-path=src src/server.js` (watches the whole source tree), or mention the limitation in the README.

completed.summary:
I checked the README changes against the running app. Most of the new text holds. All 8 code blocks of "Reproducing A1–A7 by hand" were extracted mechanically and run in order against a fresh `npm start` on port 3000 with the default database. They were run on Node 22 (plain bash, then `set -e -u -o pipefail`), Node 20.20.2 and Node 24.22.3 (strict). Every run exited with code 0, and after masking timings and paths the outputs were identical across all runs. Every output matched its comment: 7xEAST/4xWEST, identical 404 bodies, 7 certificates / 8 audit events / `{"items":[]}`, then 201 false/true/true, 1, 2, 10, 10, the 409, "first result intact", the A4 table with EAST-0000009/0000010, the two reference times, 25481 lines, "ties in ascending id order", list requests at 5-10 ms during exports, and the A7 counts.

All 7 listed known defects reproduced as described. A 20,000-learner bulk issue built with SQL took 1.2-2.0 s on a machine with load average about 6, holding a list request up for the same time. One first run took 5.4 s, but that did not repeat, so it is not reported. The other defects are listed in the checks below.

Other changes that hold:
- All 7 anchor links resolve to GitHub-style heading slugs.
- Relative `DB_PATH`, `STATIC_DIR` and `--db` typed in a subdirectory resolve there.
- The three bracketed texts of the "cannot be written to" troubleshooting entry are each produced by the server, `db:reset` and `generate:east`.
- The read-only test takes the setpriv path. Without setpriv, the nobody path works from a copy nobody can read, and it is reported as skipped with its reason where neither works.
- The test counts are right: 191 API and 253 UI tests, 0 skipped.
- The sample bulk-issue label matches a real response field for field.
- The startup order holds: no database file is left after a bad PORT or a busy port.
- `npm run dev` without dependencies prints one line and exits 1. With the port taken, it prints the API's one line and exits 1.
- The Chinese summary agrees with the English text.
- No leftover "190"/"252"/"three of its five" or old wording.

What does not hold (all minor or nit):
- **A5 block** shows the two reference times but not local-date ordering.
- **A1 block** never tries the export across tenants, and checks "nothing written" only on East's side.
- **Wrong `STATIC_DIR`**: the server starts API-only and tells the user to run `npm start`, which they just did. This contradicts the "nothing starts" sentence.
- **Refused `db:reset` hint**: the known-defect entry understates it. The hint actually advises deleting the database and its -wal, which section 9 warns against.

- **A7 block** does not show the status change.

Cleanup: every process I started (servers on 3000, 7400, 7402, 7403, 7404, 7409; npm start runs on Node 20, 22 and 24) was stopped by PID or process group. Only ports 2024, 37265 and 42299 still listen, none of them mine, and port 3000 no longer answers. I deleted /tmp/a2-1..20.json, /tmp/e1.csv, /tmp/e2.csv and /tmp/readme-claims-nb. Everything else is under scratchpad/final3/readme-claims.

All exit 0; outputs diffed after masking timings: identical; every output compared with its comment (about 30 commented outputs)

findings.title: A5 hand step does not demonstrate local-date ordering, only the two reference times
findings.description: SPEC A5 also requires that 'List sorting and CSV export must use the tenant-local calendar date'. The block makes no list-sort request. For the export it prints only `head -3` (header plus EAST-0000001/0000002, WEST-0000001/0000002). In the demo data the rows come in the same order whether sorted by tenant-local date, by UTC instant or by id: the full East list sorted by issued asc is ids 1..7 in that order. So the comment 'ordered and printed by the Sydney date' cannot be checked from what the block shows. Only the printed local wall-clock time is demonstrated.
findings.reproduction: Ran the extracted A5 block (4 runs: Node 20, 22, 22 strict, 24). Output: issuedLocal 2026-01-11 00:30 and 2026-01-10 21:30, then 2 CSV rows per tenant. Then `curl -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' '/api/certificates?sort=issued&order=asc&pageSize=100'` lists ids 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 with UTC instants and local dates in the same order, so no row pair separates local-date ordering from UTC ordering.

findings.title: A1 hand step skips the export and checks 'nothing written' only on East's side
findings.description: SPEC A1 names list, detail, bulk issue and export, and says the cross-tenant bulk issue must be rejected 'without creating certificates or audit events'. The block never runs an export as Bob. After Bob's rejected bulk issue it counts only East's certificates (7), East's audit events (8) and East's operations. It never counts the actor's own tenant (West: certificates, audit events, operations), which is where a leaky implementation would most likely write rows on Bob's behalf. The West list is shown only before the bulk issue.
findings.reproduction: Ran the extracted A1 block 4 times. The outputs are 7 x EAST, 4 x WEST (before the POST), 404/404/404, then `"total":7`, `"total":8` and `{"items":[]}`, all from Alice's view. No request in the block uses export.csv, and no request after the POST uses $B.
findings.expected: The A1 block also shows Bob's export containing only WEST rows, and West's certificate/audit/operation counts unchanged after the rejected bulk issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv" | cut -d, -f3 | sort | uniq -c` and, after the POST, Bob's `?pageSize=1` total (4), `/api/audit-events` total and `/api/bulk-issues` (empty).

findings.title: A STATIC_DIR that does not exist is accepted silently, and the page then gives the wrong fix
findings.description: README section 1 says 'A value that cannot be used is reported in one line and nothing starts', and documents STATIC_DIR as the directory with the built UI. A STATIC_DIR with a typo is not refused. The server starts, logs 'Note: frontend build not found - serving the API only.' without naming the directory it looked in, and answers / with 200: 'The API is running, but the frontend has not been built yet. Run "npm start" from the repository root.' The user has just done exactly that: `npm start` built frontend/dist, but the server is looking at the typo. Following the advice changes nothing.
findings.reproduction: In my copy: `STATIC_DIR=fronted/dist PORT=7409 HOST=127.0.0.1 npm start`. The build succeeds, the server logs the note, and `curl http://127.0.0.1:7409/` returns 200 with the 'Run "npm start" from the repository root' text. The same happens with `STATIC_DIR=/nonexistent node backend/src/server.js`.
findings.expected: Either refuse an explicitly set STATIC_DIR that does not exist or has no index.html (one line, nothing starts, as the README promises for unusable values), or at least name the directory in the note and in the page text.
findings.suggestedFix: In loadConfig/server start-up, when STATIC_DIR is set, check that <dir>/index.html exists and fail with 'STATIC_DIR ... contains no built UI'. Otherwise print the resolved path in the note.

findings.title: Known defect 'hint about damaged files that does not apply' understates it: the hint tells the user to delete the database and its -wal
findings.description: After a refused `npm run db:reset` on a database that is merely not writable, the second line reads 'If the file is damaged, stop the server and delete <db>* to start over.' Deleting <db>* removes the database itself and any -wal file, which can hold committed data. Section 9 warns explicitly that a left-over -wal 'can hold data' and should be made writable, not deleted. The defect list calls the hint merely inapplicable. In the read-only -wal case it actually advises the data-losing action the troubleshooting section forbids.
findings.reproduction: `setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override npm run -s db:reset -- --db ro/b/x.sqlite` with a 0444 x.sqlite-wal next to the database prints: 'Reset failed, nothing was changed: the database cannot be written to (the file x.sqlite-wal next to it is read-only for this user)' / 'If the file is damaged, stop the server and delete .../ro/b/x.sqlite* to start over.' The same hint is printed for a read-only file (ro/a) and a read-only directory (ro/c).
findings.expected: The known-defect entry says the hint suggests deleting the database files, contradicting section 9, or the hint is suppressed for 'cannot be written to' errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not print the delete hint when the error message starts with 'the database cannot be written to'; failing that, reword the README entry.

findings.title: Hand steps assume the second terminal is in the project folder, but do not say so
findings.description: The prose says 'start it as in section 1, then use a second terminal'. The first block starts with `npm run db:reset`, and A6 uses `npm run generate:east`. Both fail outside the project tree, and a new terminal usually opens in the home directory. In a non-strict shell the remaining blocks keep running on data that was not reset. A6 then measures exports of 10 rows and cannot show the documented 25,481 lines.
findings.reproduction: `cd /tmp/somewhere-else && npm run db:reset` prints 'npm error code ENOENT ... path /tmp/somewhere-else/package.json' and exits 254.
findings.expected: 'then, in a second terminal in the project directory, ...' (or a `cd` line in the first block).
findings.suggestedFix: Add 'in the project directory' to the sentence, or start the first block with a comment `# in the repository root`.

findings.title: Hand steps leave /tmp/a2-1..20.json and /tmp/e1.csv, /tmp/e2.csv behind, unmentioned
findings.description: A2 writes 20 files /tmp/a2-*.json, and A6 writes two CSVs of about 1.9 MB each to /tmp. The README neither mentions them nor gives a clean-up line, and the steps silently overwrite any existing files with those names.
findings.reproduction: After a run: `ls -la /tmp/a2-*.json /tmp/e*.csv` lists 22 files: twenty of 1278 bytes and /tmp/e1.csv, /tmp/e2.csv of 1,925,512 bytes each.
findings.expected: A closing `rm -f /tmp/a2-*.json /tmp/e1.csv /tmp/e2.csv`, or a sentence saying the files are left there.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the rm line at the end of A6 (or the end of the subsection).

findings.title: A2 'all twenty answers are the same' check cannot detect requests that failed
findings.description: `sort -u /tmp/a2-*.json | wc -l` prints 1 as long as the files that do exist are identical. A request that never got an answer leaves no file (curl -o writes nothing on a connection error), and an empty file adds no line. A failed request, or stale files from an earlier run, therefore still produce '1'. The HTTP statuses of the 20 concurrent calls are not shown either.
findings.reproduction: In a scratch directory: a2-1.json with content plus an empty a2-2.json gives `sort -u a2-*.json | wc -l` = 1. `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7449/x -o a2-3.json` (nothing listening) exits 7 and creates no file, and the count is still 1.
findings.expected: A check that also shows that 20 answers exist, for example `cat /tmp/a2-*.json | wc -l` or `ls /tmp/a2-*.json | wc -l` = 20, or curl -w '%{http_code}' collected per request.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `ls /tmp/a2-*.json | wc -l   # 20` and delete old /tmp/a2-*.json before the xargs line.

findings.title: A7 hand step shows the alreadyRevoked flag but not the status change
findings.description: SPEC A7: 'Revoking a valid certificate changes its status and writes 1 audit event.' The block greps only `alreadyRevoked` and the audit actions. `"status":"revoked"` is in the response but is filtered out, so the status change is inferred rather than shown.
findings.reproduction: Ran the A7 block 4 times: output is `"alreadyRevoked":false`, `"alreadyRevoked":true`, then 1 certificate.issued and 1 certificate.revoked. The status field never appears in the output.
findings.expected: One line that shows status active before the revoke and revoked after it (for example `grep -o '"status":"[a-z]*"' | head -1` on GET /api/certificates/3).
findings.suggestedFix: Add `curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/3" | grep -o '"status":"[a-z]*"' | head -1` before and after the revoke.
